topic: Working from the couch: a better laptop setup

slides.headline: Working from the couch again?
slides.sub: You don't need a home office. A few swaps go a long way.

slides.title: The couch problem
slides.body: Soft cushions let you sink, and the laptop ends up on your knees. Your head drifts down towards the screen, and after an hour or so your neck and lower back let you know.

slides.title: Raise the screen
slides.body: Put the laptop on a firm cushion, a lap desk or a stack of books so the screen sits closer to eye level. Every few centimetres of height takes load off your neck.

slides.title: Add a cheap keyboard
slides.body: Once the screen is raised, typing gets awkward. A wireless keyboard and mouse let you keep the screen up and your arms relaxed. A small cost for a noticeable difference.

slides.title: Back into the corner
slides.body: Sit into the arm of the couch with a cushion behind your lower back, or move to the dining table for focused work. Changing spots through the day is a good thing.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain spreading into an arm or leg, pins and needles, headaches that keep building, or stiffness that isn't easing after a week or two are worth an assessment.

slides.headline: Sore from the home office?
slides.body: Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios look at your setup and how you move, then give you a simple plan to follow. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
The couch is comfy for the first 20 minutes. Then your neck starts talking. 🛋️

Laptops on laps pull your head down and forward, and soft cushions let your lower back sag. You don't need a full home office to improve things: raise the screen on a firm cushion or books, add a cheap wireless keyboard and mouse, and sit into the corner of the couch with a cushion behind your back.

Better still, switch spots through the day. The dining table, the couch and a standing bench all have their place.

story.headline: Laptop on the couch?
story.body: Prop the screen on books, add a cheap keyboard, and sit into the corner with a cushion behind you.
